title: The Last Thorn Again
premise: Cyrus Dravenmoor has spent a decade poisoning herself in small doses as the crown's food-taster, learning every smuggler's path through the Thornfell mountains while staying deliberately unremarkable. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin to be answered, she discovers her immunity was never accidental: she is the last heir of the covenant that once bound dragon-fire, divine favor, and mortal law together, and her body has been quietly rebuilt to carry it. Hunted by a chancellor who wants the gods' power monopolized for the throne, Cyrus must cross Thornfell with smugglers, a disgraced priestess, and a half-starved dragon to reforge the broken covenant at the First Hearth. She succeeds only by surrendering her hard-won invisibility and accepting that survival bought at the cost of belonging was never survival at all.
about_author: Xanthe Halloran is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons mapping passes through real mountain ranges before turning them into fictional ones. Their work blends folkloric fantasy with intimate, unsentimental character studies of people who survive by being overlooked.

chapters.title: A Pinch of Nightshade
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She tastes a suspect dish at court, identifies arsenic laced with something older, and saves the king without anyone noticing she exists. Establishes her immunity, her invisibility as armor, and her secret knowledge of Thornfell's smuggler roads. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into loneliness.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A kitchen scullery maid prays to a dead god over a burnt stew—and the stew unmakes itself. Cyrus witnesses it, feels her own scars burn in answer, and realizes the old gods are waking. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a terrible, unfamiliar hope.

chapters.title: What the Immunity Was For
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She breaks into the palace archive and finds her own hiring record falsified twenty years ago; her poisoning regimen was a ritual, not medicine. Someone has been building her into a vessel since childhood. Emotional beat: betrayal—the one thing she trusted, her own body, was never hers.

chapters.title: Chancellor Veyra's Garden
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The chancellor tends a greenhouse of godsbane plants and reveals to her spymaster that she knows exactly what Cyrus is becoming—and intends to harvest the covenant's power for the crown alone. Emotional beat: chilling competence masking genuine fear of what the gods want in return.

chapters.title: Run the Thorn Road
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Fleeing arrest, Cyrus uses smuggler paths only she knows, guided by an old map tattooed on her mother's recipe cards. She falls in with a caravan led by the smuggler Sefa, who owes her mother a debt. Emotional beat: exhilaration of flight shadowed by grief for the life she can't return to.

chapters.title: The Priestess Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In a mountain shrine she finds Maera, a disgraced priestess who drank the river Lethe-water to forget her failures. The waking gods are restoring Maera's memories against her will, painfully. Cyrus must decide whether healing someone means forcing them to remember. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: Embers Below the Ice
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The caravan detours to a frozen lake where Sefa trades with something ancient: a dragon, Ashvane, last keeper of the covenant's fire, now guttering toward death. Sefa bargains passage in exchange for a favor unnamed. Emotional beat: awe and the unease of debts you can't measure.

chapters.title: The Dragon Remembers Her Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Ashvane recognizes Cyrus's bloodline and speaks her true family name aloud—Dravenmoor of the First Hearth—for the first time in her life. The naming physically changes her; she can no longer pass unnoticed anywhere. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo of finally being seen.

chapters.title: Veyra Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Using the falsified records, Veyra brands Cyrus a poisoner and heretic, turning public fear of the waking gods into a manhunt. We see Veyra genuinely believe she is saving the realm from divine caprice. Emotional beat: righteous conviction becoming indistinguishable from tyranny.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Justice
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A bounty hunter infiltrates the caravan; the smugglers hold their own trial in a hollowed-out cairn. Cyrus refuses to let them kill him, exposing herself as more than cargo. Sefa begins to see her as kin rather than debt. Emotional beat: first taste of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Maera's Memory Returns
chapters.summary: Maera's POV. Full recall floods back: Maera was the priestess who broke the covenant decades ago, bribed by the crown, believing she was preventing a god-war. Her guilt explains everything—including why the gods went silent and why they're angry now. Emotional beat: devastation transmuting into resolve to make amends.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Ambushed on a ridge, Cyrus must choose between saving the caravan or the covenant's relic, the Hearthstone shard. She chooses the people—her first act of belonging over duty—and loses the shard to Veyra's agents. Emotional beat: grief that is also, strangely, relief.

chapters.title: Court of the Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Ashvane's POV. Inside the dragon's dying memory, Cyrus relives the original covenant-making: three realms, one hearth, freely given. She learns the covenant cannot be reforged with the stolen shard—it must be remade by consent, which is why Veyra's theft can never work. Emotional beat: understanding that power hoarded is power lost.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. One of the old gods answers a desperate prayer directly, offering Cyrus vengeance on Veyra in exchange for sole dominion over the new covenant. She recognizes the trap her whole life trained her for: easy power, paid in others' freedom. Emotional beat: temptation resisted at real cost—a companion is hurt covering her refusal.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Capital
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra attempts to ignite the stolen shard in the palace hearth; it burns cold and begins siphoning the city's warmth instead. Panic spreads as the waking gods withdraw even the small mercies. Emotional beat: Veyra's control fracturing, doubling down rather than repenting.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The company climbs toward the First Hearth through a killing storm, Ashvane too weak to fly. Each member gives up something: Sefa her hoarded gold, Maera her forgetting, Cyrus her final vial of antidotes—choosing vulnerability over armor. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the true currency of belonging.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hearth Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The rescued bounty hunter sells their route to Veyra; soldiers seize the gate. Maera offers herself as ransom, confessing her ancient crime publicly to buy time. Cyrus watches the woman she healed choose consequence over escape. Emotional beat: fury and admiration entwined.

chapters.title: The Last Thorn
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax begins: inside the First Hearth, Cyrus confronts Veyra amid the dying flame. Veyra argues the gods abandoned mortals once already; Cyrus counters that mortals broke the bargain first. Ashvane arrives, spending her final strength to shield them. Emotional beat: two worldviews colliding with neither wholly wrong.

chapters.title: Reforge
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax resolves: the covenant accepts not blood but consent—so Cyrus offers not obedience but partnership, speaking for the human realm while Maera speaks for the gods and the freed bounty hunter, converted by what he's witnessed, stands witness for the lawless. The flame takes all three voices. Veyra, offered a place, refuses and is unmade by the fire she tried to own. Emotional beat: transcendence earned through shared cost.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Maera's POV. Aftermath: Ashvane dies content, her ember passing into the First Hearth; Maera takes up her priesthood again, carrying both guilt and forgiveness. The gods return not as miracles but as presence—answers that ask questions back. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace.

chapters.title: A Seat at the Table
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Back at court, Cyrus declines a crown-adjacent title and instead founds a guild of tasters, healers, and road-speakers—people skilled at surviving, now skilled at belonging. She tastes the king's soup one last time, then hands the spoon to an apprentice. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; invisibility exchanged for chosen visibility.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Epilogue: Sefa runs the Thorn roads openly now, guild-stamped and unafraid, and finds a small dragon egg warming in the ashes of Ashvane's lake. She sends word to Cyrus: the covenant holds, and it is already growing. Final beat: the future arriving unannounced, like all good guests.
